game.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
game.setting: Leonida — Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Mount Kalaga, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and the Grassrivers
game.difficultyRating: 4/10 — a long, tidy list rather than a hard one; patience and clean bookkeeping beat fast thumbs here
game.version: Round 8 — full rewrite with a cited guide on every trophy, November 2026

roadmap.title: Phase 1 — Story First, Nothing Else
roadmap.tagline: Lucia and Jason, opening scene to credits
roadmap.brief: Play the campaign straight through before you hunt anything. Missions unlock Leonida district by district, teach the driving, shooting and partner systems every later phase leans on, and hand you twelve trophies simply for finishing chapters and named missions. At every chapter break, save manually into a fresh slot and leave that slot alone forever: two trophies on this list hinge on single story moments, and a save parked just before them turns a miss into a two-minute reload.
roadmap.focus: Finish every chapter and named mission; bank one untouched save at each chapter break.

roadmap.title: Phase 2 — Open Every Stranger Strand Early
roadmap.tagline: Six storylines that ripen while you do other things
roadmap.brief: Stranger strands unfold in instalments separated by in-game days, so the winning move is to start each one the moment its marker appears and let the waiting happen in the background of other phases. Finishing Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone pays five bronze trophies, and every strand you close also counts toward the silver Strangers & Freaks tally of eight, so an opened strand is never wasted travel.
roadmap.focus: Trigger all strands on sight; close Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone.

roadmap.title: Phase 3 — One Lap of Everything, Then the Range
roadmap.tagline: Sample the whole state, then master the scored loops
roadmap.brief: With the map open, visit each activity icon exactly once — that single lap earns Master of None and shows you which loops you enjoy. Then settle into the scored ones: gold medals across the shooting range, a drone-race win at every site, twenty race wins in total. These are short, repeatable loops, perfect for filling the dead time between stranger instalments in the middle of the hunt.
roadmap.focus: Touch every activity type once; range golds; a drone win at each location; twenty race wins.

roadmap.title: Phase 4 — Sweep Leonida Region by Region
roadmap.tagline: Beaches, swamps, summits and everything between
roadmap.brief: Exploration trophies pay for curiosity backed by a checklist. Work the state one region at a time for the meditation spots, the hundred discovered vehicles and the full map reveal, and register cars to the Scooter Bros app whenever a new model crosses your path. Do this phase while your story knowledge of the map is fresh, and keep the tracker open beside you so no region needs a second sweep.
roadmap.focus: Meditation spots, vehicle discoveries, full-map reveal, ten Scooter Bros registrations.

roadmap.title: Phase 5 — The Robbery Circuit
roadmap.tagline: Vaults, trucks, jewelry and one very loud exit
roadmap.brief: The combat block is mostly a robbery circuit: five bank vaults, an armored truck, a jewelry store taken silently, one illegal operation from each gang, and a showroom escape in classic style. Bring your partner, a fast car and a saved game before each attempt; most of these trophies forgive failure instantly, so reload and rerun rather than improvising a messy escape that costs more time than it saves.
roadmap.focus: Five vaults, the armored truck, the silent jewelry job, one operation per gang.

roadmap.title: Phase 6 — Two-Player Chores, Solo Player
roadmap.tagline: Everything the list asks of Lucia and Jason together
roadmap.brief: Three trophies need the duo working as one: losing a four-star wanted level together, robbing three shops back-to-back without dropping the heat, and the mass-appeal partnership moment. These are short set pieces rather than grinds — set them up deliberately in free roam with a planned escape route, and they fall in a single sitting between bigger phases.
roadmap.focus: One clean four-star escape together; three chained shop robberies; the partnership moment.

roadmap.title: Phase 7 — The Long Tail, Counted Honestly
roadmap.tagline: Stunts, cards, challenges and the money trophies
roadmap.brief: What remains is arithmetic: 250 stunts, fifty challenges, three collectible card sets, a hundred WAiNK spots, a quarter million laundered, a hundred thousand spent and every garage bought. The in-game stats screen counts all of it exactly, so check it weekly, aim each session at the counter furthest from its target, and never grind a number the story would have raised for free.
roadmap.focus: Chase the furthest counter first; verify progress on the stats screen, not by feel.

roadmap.title: Phase 8 — The 100% Audit and the Platinum
roadmap.tagline: A Long Road first, then the receipt prints itself
roadmap.brief: Close the hunt with the gold A Long Road: audit the in-game 100% checklist line by line against this tracker until both agree nothing is missing. When the fifty-fourth trophy lands, Vice Got a Price! follows on its own — there is nothing to claim, press or buy. If a counter disagrees with the tracker, trust the game screen and hunt the gap; it is always a real, findable thing.
roadmap.focus: Reconcile tracker and 100% checklist; the platinum awards itself at 54 of 55.

rules.title: Three saves, three jobs
rules.text: Keep one save parked before each chapter point of no return, one current free-roam save you actually play from, and one cold backup you touch only when something breaks. The two missable trophies both turn on single moments; with a chapter-break save behind you, a missed moment costs a reload instead of a second playthrough.

rules.title: Start the slow counters on day one
rules.text: Stunts, challenges, card sets, WAiNK spots, laundered money and shop spending all grow quietly while you play the story. Glance at the stats screen once a week and nudge whichever counter is furthest behind; a counter started in hour one is a chore finished by hour sixty, and the same counter started at the end is a wall.

rules.title: Open strands the hour they appear
rules.text: Stranger missions ripen in instalments separated by in-game days. Triggering a strand early costs two minutes and lets its waiting period run underneath everything else you do; triggering it late means standing around at the end of the hunt, watching a clock that could have been ticking all along.

rules.title: Tick it the day it pops
rules.text: Mark every trophy in this tracker the moment it lands, and once per roadmap phase compare the tracker count against the PlayStation trophy screen. A trophy earned quietly and hunted twice is the purest waste in any platinum run; two minutes of bookkeeping per phase makes it impossible.

rules.title: The game screen outranks this page
rules.text: Where the shipped game and this guide disagree — a renamed spot, a moved collectible, a counter that behaves differently — the game is right and the guide is a snapshot written before release. Trust the in-game stats and 100% checklist for every number, and treat this page as the map, not the territory.

rules.title: Never buy progress you can earn
rules.text: The money trophies count money earned, laundered and spent through play. Resist any shortcut that spends real money or exploits a patched glitch: the list is long but honest, every counter on it can be filled by playing, and a platinum with an asterisk in your own head is worth less than the hours it saved.

faq.q: Can any trophy be missed for good on one playthrough?
faq.a: Only two can be missed on a single pass: Actions Speak Louder, which turns on a story choice, and Bad Luck, I Guess, which asks you to fail once and then succeed. Both stay safe if you keep the chapter-break saves from the rules — reload, take the moment the other way, and carry on. Everything else on the list remains available after the credits roll.

faq.q: How long does the platinum honestly take?
faq.a: The guide estimates 85 to 110 hours: roughly a third story, a third strands, activities and exploration, and a third the counted long tail of stunts, challenges, cards and money. Starting the slow counters during the story, as the roadmap insists, is the difference between the low end of that range and the high end.

No trophy on the official list names a difficulty, and nothing in the descriptions gates an award behind a hard mode. Play on the setting you enjoy; the list tests stamina, tidiness and a little stealth on the robbery circuit, not reflexes. The difficulty dots on each card rate the trophy itself, not a setting you choose.

faq.q: Where do the trophy names and descriptions come from?
faq.a: They are the official PlayStation 5 list for Grand Theft Auto VI, reproduced exactly — including the one name with asterisks in it — and mirrored into tools/trophies-list.json by the build script. Each card then adds this guide's own cited guide text, a five-step strategy and a tip, all written for this page and labelled with their sources.

faq.q: Is there any online or multiplayer trophy to worry about?
faq.a: The official list of 55 is a single-player list: story, strands, activities, exploration, combat, partner moments between the two protagonists, and counted grinds. The partner trophies are about Lucia and Jason acting together inside the campaign and free roam, not about other players, so the whole platinum can be earned offline and alone.

faq.q: What should I do when a counter in-game disagrees with the tracker?
faq.a: Believe the game. The in-game stats and 100% checklist screens count stunts, cards, spots, challenges and money exactly, while a tracker only knows what you ticked. A disagreement always means a tick was missed or a collectible was counted twice — hunt the gap line by line; it is a real thing and it is findable.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum itself, and there is no separate task for it: it unlocks on its own the instant the other fifty-four trophies sit on your account. Plan backwards from it — clear the story with chapter-break saves banked, keep the two missables safe, start every slow counter in the first hours, and audit the endgame against the in-game 100% checklist. Nothing here can be bought, rushed or triggered early; it is a receipt for the whole list, printed the moment the list is done.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's eight-phase roadmap and platinum audit
strategy: Treat the platinum as a receipt rather than a target: it awards itself when the other fifty-four trophies are earned, so aim every hour at them and never at this one directly — there is no button, vendor or location attached to it.

Keep the tracker honest as you go: tick each trophy on the day it pops and, once per roadmap phase, reconcile the count here against the PlayStation trophy screen, so nothing earned quietly is ever hunted a second time.

Protect the hunt's two fragile points — the story choice behind Actions Speak Louder and the fail-first moment behind Bad Luck, I Guess — with chapter-break saves, and the rest of the list can never be lost on one playthrough.

In the endgame, work only from the in-game stats and 100% checklist screens: they count stunts, cards, spots, challenges and money exactly, and the distance from those numbers to their targets is your real remaining work.

When the fifty-fourth trophy lands, stay somewhere scenic for a few seconds: the platinum follows automatically, there is nothing to press or claim, and you have earned the right to watch this one arrive slowly.
trophies.tip: It awards itself — earn the other 54 and this is the receipt.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is an early story mission, and finishing it in the normal flow of Chapter 1 is the whole trophy. Play it as the campaign presents it — it doubles as the game's gentle introduction to Leonida's water and its fishing activity, which matters again later for the fishing challenge against Cal. There is no fail state that can lock this out: if the mission goes wrong, the game reloads the checkpoint and you simply finish it on the next attempt.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mission flow: this guide's story playthrough notes
strategy: Simply reach Gone Fishing in the Chapter 1 flow and play it to the end: it is a story mission, not an optional job, so following the campaign markers brings you to it without any searching or side preparation at all.

Use the mission as free tuition: it introduces the water, the boats and the fishing rhythm the game expects later, so pay attention to the prompts instead of skipping through them — the lesson pays off against Cal.

If anything goes wrong mid-mission, let the checkpoint reload happen and continue: story missions cannot be failed permanently, and the trophy only cares that the mission ends completed, not that it ended cleanly.

Do not wander off to hunt collectibles first: nothing in this mission is missable, nothing in it is timed for the trophy, and the campaign will hand you far better hunting tools a few missions later in the chapter.

When the mission-complete banner fades, glance at the tracker and tick the trophy the same minute: starting the bookkeeping habit on the very first story trophy is what keeps the endgame audit painless.
trophies.tip: A story mission — play Chapter 1 and it cannot be avoided.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the game's long welcome: it introduces Lucia and Jason, opens the first districts of Leonida and teaches every core system. Completing the chapter in the normal campaign flow earns the trophy — no choices inside it can void the award. The one habit worth starting here is the chapter-break save: when the chapter ends, park a manual save in its own slot before playing on, because later chapters contain the list's two missable moments and the discipline is easier to keep than to start.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); chapter structure: this guide's roadmap playtesting notes
strategy: Follow the campaign markers from the opening scene to the chapter card: Chapter 1 is linear in structure even when the map feels open, and completing its final mission is the entire requirement for this trophy.

Spend the chapter learning rather than hunting: driving, cover shooting, the partner switch and the wanted system all debut here, and every later phase of the roadmap assumes you are fluent in all four of them.

Resist the urge to clear side icons between missions: the map opens properly in later chapters, the best vehicles and weapons are still locked away, and anything you can find now will still be there then.

The moment the chapter completes, save manually into a brand-new slot and never overwrite it: this is the first of the chapter-break saves the rules demand, and it anchors the whole missable-protection scheme.

Tick the trophy in the tracker before starting Chapter 2, and note the time: the 4-to-6-hour pace of this chapter is the yardstick the guide's 85-to-110-hour estimate is built from, so a much slower pace hints at hunting too early.
trophies.tip: Finish the chapter, then bank the first chapter-break save.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 widens the map and the money, and its completion is all this trophy asks — the name, asterisks and all, is the official one exactly as PlayStation publishes it. Play the chapter through, and when it closes, repeat the discipline from Chapter 1: a fresh manual save in its own slot before you touch Chapter 3. Stranger markers begin appearing around this part of the campaign; open any you pass, because their instalments ripen on in-game days and early starts cost nothing.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — asterisks as published); method: this guide's roadmap playtesting notes
strategy: Play Chapter 2's missions in the order the campaign offers them and finish the chapter finale: like every chapter trophy on the list, this one is a completion award with no performance condition hidden inside it at all.

Let the chapter's wider map tempt you only briefly: a little free roam teaches the new districts, but the systematic exploration sweep belongs to Phase 4, when every tool and vehicle class is available to you.

Open any stranger strand whose marker you pass while travelling between missions: the first meeting takes minutes, and the instalment timer then runs quietly underneath the rest of your story progress.

When the chapter card appears, bank the second chapter-break save in a fresh slot before starting Chapter 3: two saves deep, the scheme that protects both missable trophies later is fully in place and costs nothing.

Tick the trophy and glance at the slow counters on the stats screen — stunts, vehicles discovered, money earned: they should already be moving, because the roadmap starts them here, not at the end of the game.
trophies.tip: Chapter completion, plain and simple — save at the break.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter 3 is the campaign's midpoint bloom, with Vice City itself fully in play, and finishing the chapter earns the trophy. By now the roadmap's background systems should all be running: stranger strands opened, slow counters moving, chapter-break saves banked. If any of those habits has slipped, this chapter break is the cheapest place to repair it — the story's second half contains the choice the missable Actions Speak Louder turns on, so arrive at it with saves and strands in order.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's roadmap playtesting notes
strategy: Complete Chapter 3's mission chain through its finale: the trophy is the chapter-completion award, and nothing about how stylishly or slowly you play the missions changes whether it lands at the chapter card.

Use this chapter's travel time productively: register new vehicles to the Scooter Bros app as they appear, take stunt jumps you pass rather than detouring for them, and let the counted grinds grow underneath the story.

Check your stranger strands at the chapter break: any strand opened in Chapter 2 should have a fresh instalment waiting, and closing instalments promptly keeps the eight-strand silver on schedule without a dedicated grind.

Bank the third chapter-break save in its own untouched slot the moment the chapter ends: the story's second half holds the choice behind the missable Actions Speak Louder, and this save discipline is its insurance.

Tick the trophy, compare the tracker against the PlayStation screen for the first time if you have not yet, and correct any drift now — drift found at the halfway point costs minutes, drift found at the end costs hours.
trophies.tip: Midpoint chapter — finish it with saves and strands in order.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 carries the campaign toward its endgame, and completing it earns this trophy in the usual way. The practical work at this break is preparation: the final mission trophy and the story-choice missable both sit ahead, so confirm your chapter-break saves are intact, your wanted-level escape routes are practised, and your money counters are healthy. Nothing in Chapter 4 itself can be missed — the trophy is a completion award, and the chapter can always be finished from a checkpoint reload.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's roadmap playtesting notes
strategy: Play Chapter 4 to its closing mission and take the chapter card: as with the earlier chapters, the award is for completion, and checkpoint reloads along the way carry no penalty for the trophy or for anything after it.

Treat this chapter break as the endgame rehearsal: confirm each chapter-break save still sits in its own slot, untouched, because the remaining story holds both the finale and the choice the missable list cares about.

Top up the practical skills the finale will assume: losing a wanted level cleanly, switching between the protagonists under pressure, and driving the long causeways without swimming — all cheaper to practise now than mid-finale.

Glance at the money trophies' progress on the stats screen: laundering and spending should be well advanced by now, and if either lags, the remaining free roam between chapters is the natural place to feed it.

Bank the chapter-break save, tick the trophy, and reconcile the tracker with the PlayStation screen: from here the roadmap leaves the story phase, and a clean ledger is the ticket into everything after.
trophies.tip: Finish Chapter 4 and rehearse the endgame at its break.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold is for finishing the campaign's final mission, whenever you choose to play it. The roadmap deliberately leaves it flexible: some hunters finish the story first and hunt in the post-game, others clear side content before the finale — both work, because the mission stays available and nothing after it locks. Before you start it, make one fresh manual save; after the credits, that save is your clean way back to any pre-finale moment the missable list might still need.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's roadmap playtesting notes
strategy: Start the final mission whenever your hunt is ready for the credits: it remains available after every other phase, nothing in the post-game locks behind it, and the gold pays simply for completing it, however you arrive.

Make one fresh manual save immediately before launching it, in a new slot: that save is your permanent bridge back to the pre-finale world, and it is the last piece of the chapter-break save scheme the rules describe.

Go in stocked rather than fast: full health supplies, your best vehicles ready and both protagonists' loadouts sensible — the finale is the campaign's longest single run, and preparation is the whole difficulty.

If a sequence defeats you, take the checkpoint reload without frustration: retries cost minutes, and the trophy makes no distinction between a flawless finale and one finished on the fifth attempt at a hard corner.

Watch the credits, let the game return you to free roam, then tick the gold and save again in the post-game: every remaining trophy on the list is earnable from here, and the roadmap's later phases now have the whole map.
trophies.tip: The finale, finished once — save just before you launch it.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and completing it during the campaign is the whole requirement. It sits in the story flow rather than on the open map, so there is nothing to find and nothing to prepare: follow the mission markers when it arrives, play it through its checkpoints, and the trophy lands with the mission-complete banner. A failed attempt simply reloads — no choice or outcome inside the mission can spend this trophy, and it cannot be skipped past by accident.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mission flow: this guide's story playthrough notes
strategy: Play Breakfast Run when the campaign hands it to you and finish it: it is a named story mission on the critical path, so it cannot be missed, skipped or locked out by anything you do before or after it.

Treat the mission as a systems lesson like the other early named missions: whatever vehicle, route or partner mechanic it showcases will be assumed knowledge later, so follow its prompts rather than brute-forcing your own way through.

Take checkpoint reloads freely if a section goes wrong: the trophy records completion only, and a messy finish pays exactly the same bronze as a perfect one — save your perfectionism for the scored activities.

Do not detour mid-mission for collectibles or counters: the mission's world state is temporary, progress made inside story spaces does not always persist, and free roam right afterwards is the honest place to hunt.
Tick the trophy when the mission banner fades and carry on with the chapter: the named-mission bronzes are the list's simplest entries, and their only real job is keeping your tracker habit warm.
trophies.tip: A named story mission — finish it when it arrives.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is the campaign's big set-piece robbery, and completing the mission earns the trophy. It is also the template for the whole robbery circuit in Phase 5 — vault work, crowd control and a hot escape — so play it attentively rather than merely surviving it. Approach choices inside the mission change how it plays, not whether it pays: any route that reaches the mission-complete banner counts, and checkpoints forgive experiments, so try the loud and quiet approaches across reloads if you like.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mission flow: this guide's story playthrough notes
strategy: Complete The Cartel Heist in the story flow: it is a campaign centrepiece, reached by following the markers, and the trophy pays on the mission-complete banner regardless of the approach you chose inside it.

Study the heist as the robbery circuit's tutorial: the vault routine, the escape timing and the wanted-level management it teaches are exactly the skills the five bank vaults and the armored truck will test later.

Experiment across checkpoint reloads if a section interests you: heist missions usually support more than one approach, and learning both the loud and the quiet way now is free training for the silent jewelry job.
Keep your spending boring until the heist is done: arrive with health, armour and a decent getaway-capable car already owned, because mid-mission shopping trips are where clean runs go to die.

Tick the trophy at the banner, then bank a save: the heist tends to move the story's money and heat state significantly, and a save here preserves a useful before-and-after pair for later experiments.
trophies.tip: Finish the story heist — it is the robbery circuit's tutorial.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission; finishing it in the campaign flow earns the trophy, with no hidden condition. Like the other named-mission bronzes it cannot be missed or failed permanently — checkpoints carry you through a rough attempt. Its real value in the hunt is pacing: these mid-campaign missions are where the roadmap asks you to confirm the background systems are alive — strands ripening, counters moving, saves banked — because the story only gets denser from here.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mission flow: this guide's story playthrough notes
strategy: Complete Child's Play when the campaign presents it: a named story mission, finished once, is the entire requirement, and no performance grade, time limit or choice inside it touches the award at all.

Use the mission's quieter stretches to practise the partner mechanics it leans on: the duo systems debut gently here and are tested hard by the partner trophies later, so fluency bought cheaply now is valuable.

Reload checkpoints without a second thought if a section beats you twice: the trophy cannot tell a first-try finish from a fifth-try one, and stubbornness is the only way this mission can waste your time.

When the banner fades, spend sixty seconds on housekeeping: tick the trophy, check which stranger instalments have ripened during the mission, and start any that are ready before returning to the story.
Save at the next natural break in a fresh slot if this mission closed a chapter beat: the chapter-break scheme only works if it is boring and automatic, never a decision you renegotiate each time.
trophies.tip: Finish the named mission; use its break for housekeeping.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission and completing it pays this bronze — nothing more exotic is hiding in the all-caps name. Play it in the campaign flow, lean on checkpoints when a set piece goes sideways, and tick it at the banner. Missions like this are the spine of Phase 1: the roadmap asks for a straight story run first precisely because a dozen trophies, this one included, fall simply for finishing the campaign's named beats in order.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mission flow: this guide's story playthrough notes
strategy: Finish Headliners in the story flow: the trophy is a completion award for a named campaign mission, reachable only by playing the campaign and impossible to lock out with any earlier decision you have made.

Pay attention to any new system the mission showcases — a vehicle class, a location type, a way the wanted system escalates — because named missions are how the game teaches, and the exam is always a later trophy.

If the mission's hardest sequence costs you several lives, change one variable per attempt — vehicle, approach angle, which protagonist leads — rather than repeating the identical run and hoping for kinder luck.
Resist pausing the story here to grind: you are mid-campaign, the map and tools are still incomplete, and every grind available now becomes faster and better paid after the credits than it is today.
Tick the bronze at the mission banner and roll straight on: Phase 1's rhythm is story, save, tick, story — and the hunters who keep that rhythm are the ones whose endgame audit takes minutes.
trophies.tip: Another named mission — finish it and keep the rhythm.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is the airport mission, and finishing it earns the trophy. Learn its ground well while you are here: the airport is also the stage for Catch Me If You Can, the unscheduled-departure trophy in the combat phase, and a hunter who knows VCIA's roads, fences and sightlines from this mission will set that moment up in minutes later. Completion is the only condition — approach, vehicle and body count are all your own business.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); airport layout: Rockstar's official Leonida pages and this guide's playthrough notes
strategy: Complete VCIA Takedown in the campaign flow: the trophy pays on the mission-complete banner, and like every named-mission bronze it cannot be missed, failed permanently or voided by an earlier choice.

While the mission walks you through the airport, memorise the ground: perimeter roads, service entrances, where the fences break and where the sightlines run long — this airfield hosts another trophy later.

That later trophy is Catch Me If You Can, the unscheduled departure: every minute of attention you pay to VCIA's layout during this mission is a minute saved when you return to stage an escape from it.

Drive the mission's vehicles properly rather than treating them as disposable: airport sequences tend to mix ground and air, and the handling you learn here is the handling the departure trophy quietly assumes.

Tick the trophy at the banner and, if the mission ended a chapter beat, bank the chapter-break save before continuing: the scheme is automatic by now, and automatic is exactly what protects the endgame.
trophies.tip: Finish the airport mission — and memorise VCIA for later.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is one of the campaign's heavier named missions, and completing it earns this bronze. At 40 to 60 minutes it is also a good final exam for Phase 1: driving, shooting, partner work and wanted management in one long run. Nothing inside it is missable and checkpoints forgive failure, so treat difficulty spikes as tuition. When it ends, the story phase of the roadmap is nearly complete — confirm your saves and tracker before the finale sequence begins.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mission flow: this guide's story playthrough notes
strategy: Complete Operation Savage Glory in the story flow: the last of the named-mission bronzes before the finale, paid purely for finishing, with checkpoint reloads carrying no penalty of any kind against the award.

Prepare like it is a finale: full supplies, sensible loadouts for both protagonists and your most reliable car staged nearby — at up to an hour, this mission punishes improvisation more than any earlier named beat.

Notice how the mission chains the game's systems together — a drive, a fight, a partner sequence, an escape — because that chain is the whole game in miniature, and fluency here is fluency everywhere after.

If one sequence walls you, vary the approach rather than the effort: a different vehicle, a different lead protagonist or a different entry angle solves more story walls than raw repetition ever does.

At the banner, do the full break routine: tick the trophy, bank a save in a fresh slot, reconcile the tracker count with the PlayStation screen — the finale and the post-game phases all start from this ledger.
trophies.tip: The heaviest named mission — prepare, finish, reconcile.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold asks for the game's own 100% completion — the checklist the in-game stats screen tracks, line by line. Work it as an audit, not a vibe: open the checklist, compare every line against this tracker, and hunt only the lines that disagree. Most hunters find their missing percent is a handful of small things — a few stunts, a strand instalment, a region unrevealed — rather than one big omission. This gold usually lands near the very end of the hunt, just before the platinum receipt.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); counts: the in-game stats and 100% checklist screens
strategy: Work from the game's own 100% checklist, not from memory: open the stats screen, read every line against this tracker, and make a short list of only the lines that disagree — that list is the entire remaining job.

Expect the gap to be small and scattered: a few stunts here, a strand instalment there, one region never fully revealed — 100% hunts are almost never missing a cathedral, they are missing a handful of bricks.

Clear the gap lines in geographic order rather than checklist order: group what remains by district, sweep each district once with the tracker open, and the audit closes without a single wasted cross-map trip.

Reconcile as you go: after each sweep, re-open the checklist and watch the percentage move — if a completed item did not move it, you have found a counting subtlety early, while it is still cheap to understand.

When the checklist reads a clean 100%, the gold lands by itself: tick it, save, and look at what remains — by construction, almost nothing stands between this moment and the platinum but the last counted trophies.
trophies.tip: Audit the in-game checklist line by line — the gap is small.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Two hundred and fifty completed stunts sounds like a wall and behaves like a garden: it grows while you do everything else, provided you start early. Take every stunt jump you pass during the story and the exploration sweep instead of promising to return — returns are where stunt counts go to die. The in-game stats screen counts completions exactly, so check it whenever a session ends. Saved for the end, this is a 6-to-10-hour grind; spread across the hunt, most of it never feels like work at all.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 250); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Start on day one and never stop: take every stunt opportunity the world puts in your path during story travel and exploration, because 250 completions gathered incidentally is a pleasure and 250 gathered in a dedicated week is not.

Learn what counts as a completion early: a stunt registers when the game says it does — a clean landing in the target zone — so favour reliable, repeatable jumps over spectacular one-offs while you build the habit and the count.

Work region by region during the exploration phase: sweep a district's stunts in one pass with the map open, tick the district off, and move on — scattered stunt hunting doubles the travel and halves the completions per hour.

Check the stats screen at the end of every session and write the number into your routine: a counter you can see growing needs no motivation, and a counter you cannot see is the one that stalls at 190 forever.

Finish the tail deliberately: when the count passes 200, dedicate short sessions to the densest remaining clusters until the silver lands — the last fifty go fastest as a focused sweep, not as background noise.
trophies.tip: Start stunts in hour one; the stats screen keeps the count.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity once — that is the entire trophy, and it is secretly the best scouting mission on the list. One lap of the activity icons shows you the shooting range, the drone races, the fishing, the arcade and everything else the later activity trophies will grade you on, while the grading is still free. Do the lap early in Phase 3, note which loops you genuinely enjoy, and let that preference order the silver hunts that follow: range golds and race wins are much easier in activities you like.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); activity set: Rockstar's official GTA VI pages and trailers
strategy: Make one deliberate lap of the map's activity icons, trying each distinct type exactly once: the trophy counts types attempted, not skill shown, so a cheerful failure at each new activity still moves the counter forward.

Treat the lap as reconnaissance for the expensive trophies: the range, the drone races, the fishing and the races all have graded trophies later, and this is your free look at each one's shape, controls and difficulty.

Take notes like a scout, not a tourist: which activities you enjoyed, which you were instantly good at, which felt like work — that honest ranking decides the order you hunt the activity silvers and bronzes afterwards.
Do the lap in one or two sittings early in Phase 3: scattered attempts across weeks get forgotten and repeated, while a single lap leaves a clean mental map of the whole activity layer of Leonida.

Tick the bronze when the last type registers, then start the graded hunts with your favourite: momentum is a real resource in a 100-hour hunt, and spending the first activity hours on a loop you enjoy banks it.
trophies.tip: One lap, every activity type once — free scouting for later.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold in every Shooting Range challenge is the activity list's real skill test. Work challenge by challenge: learn each one's target pattern at bronze pace, then chase gold once the rhythm is in your hands — accuracy streaks, not raw speed, are what range scoring rewards in this series. Rest between attempts; tired aim grinds slower than fresh aim. The range also quietly trains the gun handling the robbery circuit assumes, so these hours pay twice. When one challenge resists, move to another and return — patterns settle overnight.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); range format: series precedent from GTA V's shooting ranges, applied in this guide's method
strategy: Take the challenges one at a time and finish each before moving on: every range challenge has its own target pattern and scoring rhythm, and gold comes from learning one pattern deeply rather than skimming them all.

Learn at bronze pace first: run a new challenge slowly, watch where targets appear and in what order, and only then chase the gold threshold — accuracy streaks, not trigger speed, are what range scoring has always rewarded.

Short sessions beat long ones: aim degrades with fatigue in a way you cannot feel happening, so three focused half-hours across three days will out-shoot one exhausted three-hour siege on the same challenge.

Rotate when walled: if a challenge refuses gold after a dozen honest attempts, go gold another one and come back tomorrow — patterns genuinely settle overnight, and returning hunters regularly gold a wall on the second try.

Count the double dividend: range hours are also robbery training, because the vault circuit later assumes exactly this gun handling under pressure — the silver is the tuition receipt as much as the prize.
trophies.tip: One challenge at a time; streaks, not speed; rest your aim.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — a win per site, not a win streak, so each location is its own small project. Learn a course with a sighting run first: drone courses punish the turn you did not know was coming far more than they punish modest speed. Bank the win, move to the next site, and never let one stubborn course eat the whole session. These races also teach Leonida's vertical geography — rooftops, causeways, canals — which the exploration phase then spends freely.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); activity set: Rockstar's official GTA VI pages and trailers
strategy: Win once at every location, treating each site as a separate small project: the trophy needs a victory per course, not a streak, so a win banked is a win kept even if the next course humiliates you.
Fly a sighting lap before racing seriously anywhere: drone courses are won by knowing the next gate before it arrives, and one slow lap spent memorising the line is worth five fast laps of surprises.
Race the course, not the other drones: hold the clean racing line, take gates in the centre, and let rivals make the mistakes — drone fields reliably beat themselves if you simply refuse to crash.
Cap any single course at a handful of attempts per session: frustration tightens thumbs, and a course that refuses you tonight will often fall to the first fresh run tomorrow, memorised line and all.
Enjoy the side payment: drone racing teaches Leonida's vertical map — rooftops, canals, causeway gaps — and that fluency is exactly what the exploration sweep and several stunt clusters spend later.
trophies.tip: A win per site; sighting lap first, clean line always.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty different race wins — different is the operative word, so farming one easy circuit twenty times earns nothing. Spread the wins across Leonida's race series as they unlock, learn each course's first corner (most races are decided there), and bring the right vehicle class rather than a favourite car. Races you lose still teach the course, so count attempts as tuition. Mixed into the activity phase, twenty wins accumulate naturally; hunted all at once at the end, they are a long evening of first corners.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); racing format: series precedent from GTA V's race series, applied in this guide's method
strategy: Win twenty different races, and underline different: the counter ignores repeat victories on a course you already own, so spread your effort across the whole race calendar instead of farming one friendly circuit.

Learn each course's first corner before anything else: in this series the opening seconds decide most races, because a clean first corner puts you in clear air while the field sorts itself out behind you.

Bring the right vehicle, not the beloved one: check what class a race suits — tight street circuits, open causeway sprints and off-road scrambles each reward different machines — and enter with the tool the course asks for.

Count losses as tuition and keep them short: a lost race still taught you the braking points and the trap corners, so debrief for ten seconds, adjust one thing, and re-enter while the course is warm in your hands.

Pace the twenty across the whole activity phase: two or three new wins a session keeps the counter honest and the driving fresh, and leaves your best attention for the range golds that share this phase.
trophies.tip: Twenty different wins — first corners and right vehicles.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a duel, not a marathon. Gone Fishing in the story taught the basics; Cal tests them. Practise the cast-and-retrieve rhythm in free fishing first until landing fish feels boring, then take the challenge: duels are lost by the one mistake made while rushing a big fish, so play the challenge patiently and let Cal make the error. The challenge can be retried freely, so treat early attempts as scouting of what Cal typically scores, and set your target from evidence.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); fishing format: this guide's story playthrough notes from Gone Fishing
strategy: Practise in free fishing before challenging Cal: cast, retrieve and land fish until the rhythm is boring, because a duel is the worst classroom — the mechanics should be muscle memory before pride enters the water.

Scout the challenge with your first attempts: learn what score Cal typically posts, what the time limit feels like and where the challenge's fish actually bite, then set your real target from that evidence.
Fish patiently once the duel starts: fishing challenges are lost by the single rushed mistake — a snapped line on the one big fish — far more often than by a slow, steady tally of ordinary catches.
Play the water you are given: if the challenge lets you choose spots or bait, favour consistency over glory — three medium fish landed beat one trophy fish hooked, played badly and lost at the boat.

Retry without tilt when Cal wins: the challenge costs nothing to re-enter, the fish have no memory, and the attempt where you finally relax is usually the attempt where the big one finally stays hooked.
trophies.tip: Practise free first; patience beats Cal, rushing loses.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — a single cabinet, played to its end, anywhere in Leonida. This is the list's lightest activity trophy and a deliberate palate cleanser in the roadmap: take it during the activity lap, pick whichever cabinet appeals, and play it through rather than sampling it. Completion is the only bar; score and style are between you and the machine. If one cabinet fights back, another counts just as well.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); activity set: Rockstar's official GTA VI pages and trailers
strategy: Find any arcade cabinet during the activity lap and play its game all the way to completion: one finished game is the whole trophy, and the island's cabinets all count equally toward it.
Pick the game that suits your hands: cabinets differ — some are reflex tests, some are puzzles — and the trophy is gloriously indifferent to which one you finish, so choose fun over prestige.
Play to the end rather than sampling: most arcade trophies are lost by walking away at eighty percent, so once you sit down, stay seated until the game itself declares itself finished.
If one cabinet walls you, switch cabinets without shame: a different game's completion pays the identical bronze, and the stubborn machine can keep its secrets for another hunter.
Take this one early as a palate cleanser between heavier hunts: fifteen cheerful minutes that bank a trophy, reset your head and remind you the list contains gifts as well as grinds.
trophies.tip: One cabinet, played to the end — the list's lightest bronze.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's stranger strand — every instalment, through to his final mission. Strands ripen in stages separated by in-game days, so the method is the roadmap's stranger rule: open Andy's strand the hour his marker appears, play each instalment as it ripens, and never leave a ready instalment sitting while you do other phases. His finale pays this bronze and also counts toward the eight completions the silver Strangers & Freaks requires, so Andy is two trophies' worth of progress in one storyline.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); strand structure: this guide's roadmap method from series precedent
strategy: Open Andy's strand the moment his marker appears on your map: stranger strands ripen in instalments divided by in-game days, and an early opening lets that waiting run underneath your other hunting for free.

Play each instalment promptly as it ripens: a ready strand left sitting is pure delay, while a strand played on arrival keeps its finale on schedule and its story fresh in your memory between sittings.

Let time pass honestly between instalments: sleep, travel and other missions all advance the in-game days, so weave Andy's pauses into the activity and exploration phases instead of standing around waiting for him.
Finish the final mission when it unlocks and take both payments: this bronze for Andy himself, and one more completion banked toward the eight the silver Strangers & Freaks counts across the state.

Tick Andy off in the tracker with a note of the date: strand bookkeeping looks trivial now and becomes essential at strand six, when three ripening storylines compete for the same evening's attention.
trophies.tip: Open Andy early, play instalments as they ripen, finish him.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's strand through its final mission. The title winks at the water, and Kenton's storyline is one of the six named stranger arcs the list singles out with its own bronze. The method is identical to every strand and worth repeating: open it early, play instalments as the in-game days ripen them, and close the finale when it offers itself. Kenton's completion also feeds the Strangers & Freaks silver tally, so finishing him is never a detour from the platinum — it is the road itself.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); strand structure: this guide's roadmap method from series precedent
strategy: Start Kenton's strand as soon as his marker shows: the instalment clock only runs once you have met him, and every day of ripening you bank early is a day the endgame does not have to wait for.

Play instalments on arrival rather than batching them: strand finales unlock off the last instalment's timer, so prompt play keeps Kenton's ending available exactly when the roadmap wants it — mid-hunt, not post-credits.

Pay attention to his water-borne world while you work: strands teach their corners of Leonida intimately, and local knowledge — channels, docks, quiet beaches — keeps paying out in exploration and stunt phases.
Close the final mission when it ripens and collect the double payment: Kenton's own bronze, plus one more of the eight completions the silver Strangers & Freaks is quietly counting on your behalf.

Record the completion in the tracker the same day: with six named strands plus the tally silver, strand bookkeeping is the one admin task that genuinely compounds if neglected, and trivial if kept current.
trophies.tip: Kenton's finale pays twice — his bronze and a silver tally.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand — the lone rider's whole storyline, through its final mission. As with every named strand, the trophy is earned by completion, and the only way to make it slow is to open it late: instalments ripen on in-game days, so an early meeting is free progress. Billy's arc also counts toward the eight completions behind Strangers & Freaks. Keep the tracker current as his instalments land; strand hunters lose more time to forgotten half-finished storylines than to any mission's difficulty.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); strand structure: this guide's roadmap method from series precedent
strategy: Meet Billy the hour his marker appears and play the opening instalment there and then: from that moment his storyline ripens on its own clock, in parallel with everything else your hunt is doing.

Return for each instalment as it becomes ready: Billy's finale only exists after the earlier beats have landed and aged, so steady prompt returns are literally the fastest possible route to this bronze.

Use the travel between instalments: strands scatter you across Leonida, so route journeys past stunt spots, unregistered vehicles and unrevealed map — the road between strand beats is hunting time, not dead time.

Finish the final mission when it offers itself and bank the pair of payments: Billy's bronze for the strand, and another completion toward the eight that the Strangers & Freaks silver demands statewide.
Tick the strand closed in the tracker and check which other strands are ripening: the strangers phase runs like a railway timetable, and the tracker is the departure board that keeps it painless.
trophies.tip: Open Billy early; his road pays a bronze and a tally mark.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight completed stranger strands, anywhere across Leonida, earn this silver. The five named strands — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — are the spine; the list needs three more from the wider cast of Leonida's oddballs, so open every stranger marker you ever pass, even ones without their own trophy. The counter is completions, not meetings: half-finished strands pay nothing here. Run the phase like a timetable — several strands ripening at once, instalments played on arrival — and the silver lands as a by-product of good scheduling.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 8 strands); strand structure: this guide's roadmap method from series precedent
strategy: Count completions, not introductions: this silver pays for eight strands finished end to end, so a map full of opened-but-idle storylines is worth exactly nothing until their finales actually land.
Build the spine from the five named strands — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each pay their own bronze as well — then find three more strands among Leonida's wider cast of beautiful oddballs.
Open every stranger marker you pass, trophy or not: the three extra strands have to come from somewhere, and a marker ignored in week one is a storyline whose ripening clock starts a week late.
Run the phase like a timetable with several strands ripening simultaneously: play whichever instalment is ready when you log in, and the in-game-day waits overlap into almost no waiting at all.

Audit the tally in the tracker whenever a strand closes: eight is a small number with a long fuse, and the hunters who miss this silver on schedule always discover a strand they swore they had finished.
trophies.tip: Eight finished strands — five named, three more from the wild.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's strand through its final mission. Randy's storyline is one of the five named stranger arcs with its own bronze, and it obeys the universal strand rules: open early, play instalments as they ripen on in-game days, finish the finale when it unlocks. His completion also counts toward the eight behind Strangers & Freaks. If Randy's marker appears while you are mid-mission elsewhere, finish what you are doing — the marker waits — but do not let a day of real play pass with it unopened.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); strand structure: this guide's roadmap method from series precedent
strategy: Open Randy's strand promptly when his marker appears: like every strand, his instalments ripen on in-game days, and the clock that ends at his finale only starts ticking once you have shaken his hand.

Play his instalments as they ripen instead of saving them up: the finale's availability is chained to the last instalment plus time, so prompt play is the difference between a mid-hunt bronze and an endgame chore.

Let his errands teach you their economy: a strand called Supply & Demand will walk you through Leonida's grey markets, and that local knowledge feeds the money trophies the grind phase counts so carefully.
Close the final mission when it unlocks and take the familiar double payment: Randy's bronze for the strand itself, and one more completion banked toward the Strangers & Freaks silver's eight.
Update the tracker before you log off: strand state is the easiest thing in the hunt to misremember, and a two-line note tonight saves a confused map-search some evening next week.
trophies.tip: Randy's finale — a bronze, a tally mark, a market lesson.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand — the last of the five named stranger arcs — through its final mission. Same discipline as his four colleagues: meet him early so the instalment clock runs under your other work, play each beat as it ripens, and close the finale when it appears. With Tyrone done, the named-strand spine of the strangers phase is complete and only three further strand completions separate you from the Strangers & Freaks silver. Tick him off and audit the tally the same evening.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); strand structure: this guide's roadmap method from series precedent
strategy: Meet Tyrone as soon as his marker joins the map: his strand ripens in instalments like the others, and an early start means his finale matures while you are busy elsewhere, costing the hunt no dedicated waiting at all.
Play each instalment on arrival: strand finales are chained to instalments plus in-game days, so the prompt hunter finishes Tyrone almost incidentally, while the batching hunter queues at the end.

Enjoy the local colour deliberately: each named strand is a guided tour of one Leonida subculture, and the hunters who rush them miss both the jokes and the geography the exploration phase later charges for.
Finish the final mission and collect the double payment one last time for a named strand: Tyrone's bronze, plus a fifth completion banked toward the eight the Strangers & Freaks silver requires.

Audit the strand tally in the tracker tonight: with the five named arcs closed, you need exactly three more completions — knowing that number precisely turns the rest of the phase into a shopping list.
trophies.tip: Tyrone closes the named five — then three strands remain.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — a full set of quiet places in a loud game. Sweep region by region during the exploration phase, pairing each region's spots with its stunts and vehicle discoveries so no district is visited twice. Spots are small and easy to walk past; when a region's count in-game disagrees with your tracker, re-walk its scenic high points and waterlines first. The last spot is the one everyone misses, and it is always in the region you were surest about.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); locations method: this guide's region-by-region exploration sweep
strategy: Sweep region by region rather than spot by spot: meditation spots share their geography with stunts, discoveries and map reveal, so one thorough pass per district serves four trophies at once and no spot requires a dedicated trip.

Slow down at the scenic places: meditation spots live where the view is — overlooks, beaches, summits, quiet water — so when the landscape makes you stop the car anyway, look around before you drive on.

Keep a per-region tally in the tracker as you go: a single number per district, checked against the game's own count where it shows one, turns the inevitable last-spot hunt from a whole-map search into one district's re-walk.

When a region disagrees with you, re-walk its high points and waterlines first: spots hide at edges — the end of a jetty, the top of a rise, the far side of a lake — far more often than they hide in town centres.

Finish with a calm audit rather than a frantic one: sit at your final candidate spots, let the meditation actually trigger and register, and only then believe the count — haste at the last spot is how hunters visit it twice.
trophies.tip: Region sweeps, scenic edges first — the last spot hides proudly.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret wants a unique animal hunted — a specific quarry, not any deer in the Grassrivers. Take the job through Bret's strand or marker, learn where the unique animal ranges, and hunt it on its own terms: time of day, approach against the wind of the game's systems, and patience at the edge of its territory. Unique hunts in this series reward tracking over chasing, so follow sign and sound rather than sprinting at movement. If the quarry escapes, it returns — reset, re-approach, and hunt it properly.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); hunting format: series precedent from Red Dead Redemption 2's legendary hunts, applied in this guide's method
strategy: Take the hunt from Bret himself and learn the brief properly: a unique animal is a specific quarry with a specific range, and hunting the wrong creature in the right swamp pays nothing at all.

Study the territory before the animal: arrive, look for the sign the game leaves — tracks, calls, disturbed ground at the range's edges — and let the evidence tell you where the quarry actually lives today.

Hunt on the animal's terms, not yours: approach slowly, use the terrain and cover the game gives you, and take the shot or the strike only when it is clean — a spooked unique quarry costs you a full reset of the hunt.

If the quarry escapes, let it: unique hunts in this series are built to be re-attempted, the animal returns to its range, and a calm second approach with everything you just learned is faster than a desperate chase.

Report back to Bret with the hunt complete and tick the bronze: his job also deepens your map knowledge of Leonida's wild interior, which the exploration and stunt phases spend for the rest of the hunt.
trophies.tip: One unique quarry — track it, do not chase it.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full collectible card sets. Sets, not singles, are the unit: a scattered ninety percent of three sets pays nothing, while three finished sets pay the silver. Pick your three sets deliberately — ideally ones whose cards cluster in regions your other phases visit anyway — and hunt set by set to completion. Track every card as you pick it up; collectible hunts are lost in the bookkeeping far more than in the finding. The game's stats screen counts your sets, so reconcile against it whenever a set should be closing.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 3 sets); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Think in sets, not cards: the silver pays for three completed sets, so three half-finished sets and a pocketful of singles are worth zero — choose your three sets and hunt each one to its last card.

Choose sets that share geography with your other work: cards cluster by region and theme, so sets living in districts your strands, stunts and exploration already visit will fill themselves half incidentally.
Record every pickup the moment it happens: collectible hunts are lost in the bookkeeping, not the finding, and a card collected but not ticked will be hunted again at full price in the endgame audit.

Finish sets one at a time in the endgame: when a set is within five cards, drop everything and close it — a nearly-done set left for later has a way of hiding its last card behind a fresh memory of having done this already.

Reconcile against the stats screen whenever a set should complete: the game counts sets exactly, and a disagreement here means a card you believe you hold is still lying in Leonida somewhere, findable and worth finding now.
trophies.tip: Three whole sets — bookkeeping is the real hunt.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK at one hundred locations — a hundred distinct spots, spread over the whole state. Like the stunts, this counter rewards the hunter who starts early: WAiNK whenever a new location presents itself during story travel, strands and exploration, and the hundred accumulates underneath the hunt. The stats screen keeps the official count. Saved for the end it is a 6-to-9-hour tour of places you have already been; gathered on the road, it is a habit — every new rooftop, jetty and lookout gets WAiNKed before you leave it.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 100 locations); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Start in the first hour and make it a reflex: whenever the hunt takes you somewhere new — a rooftop, a jetty, a summit, a stranger's backyard — WAiNK there before you leave, and the hundred builds itself.

Remember the unit is locations, not uses: WAiNK a hundred times on your favourite pier counts once, so spread the habit across the whole map exactly as the stunts and meditation sweeps teach you to travel.

Pair it with every other sweep: the exploration phase's region passes, the stunt clusters and the strand journeys all visit prime WAiNK ground, so a hunter running those phases with this counter in mind finishes it incidentally.

Check the stats screen weekly and note the number: a visible counter climbing steadily needs no motivation, while an invisible one stalls — and a stalled WAiNK count at the end is a week of re-visiting old ground.

Close the tail deliberately: past eighty, dedicate short tours to the districts your count is thinnest in, and the silver lands as the natural receipt for a well-travelled hunt rather than a separate grind.
trophies.tip: A hundred different spots — WAiNK everywhere new, early.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete fifty challenges — the game's own rolling list of tasks across driving, combat, activities and the world. Most challenges complete themselves inside other hunts: races feed driving challenges, the range feeds shooting ones, strands and exploration feed the rest. Keep the challenge list open in your routine: check it weekly, notice which categories lag, and tilt a session toward them. Deliberately hunted from zero it looks like 10 to 15 hours; audited weekly while you play everything else, the fiftieth challenge usually lands unannounced.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 50 challenges); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Let other hunts do the heavy lifting: challenges live inside every other system — races, the range, robberies, strands, exploration — so a hunter playing the whole roadmap completes most of the fifty without ever opening the list.

Audit the challenge list weekly anyway: open it, find the categories that are lagging — there are always two — and tilt one session toward each; ten minutes of steering per week is the whole management this trophy needs.

Take the free ones the day they appear: many challenges are trivially small tasks wearing a formal name, and completing them on sight keeps the count honest and the list short enough to actually read.

Never grind a challenge the story would feed: if a category grows naturally in a phase you have not reached yet, let it wait — the roadmap's order exists precisely so counted work is never done twice at two prices.

When the count nears fifty, switch to deliberate mode: read the full list, pick the handful of shortest remaining challenges regardless of category, and close the bronze in one tidy session of small satisfactions.
trophies.tip: Fifty challenges — audit weekly, let other hunts feed it.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, earn a four-star wanted level and then lose it completely — stars gone, heat escaped, both of you free. Set it up deliberately rather than hoping crime provides: pick open ground with a planned escape route — causeways, tunnels and the airport perimeter all break line of sight well — raise the heat together, then run the route and hide until the stars drain. The trophy pays on the clean escape, so the moment that matters is the last star fading with your partner still with you.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); wanted system: series precedent from GTA V, applied in this guide's method
strategy: Stage it deliberately with your partner in the car: choose open ground near a real escape route — a causeway, a tunnel run, the long airport roads — because improvised four-star escapes end in water or in custody.

Raise the heat together and keep it at four stars: the trophy wants a four-star level lost with your partner present, so commit enough mayhem to reach four, then stop adding stars and start running the plan.

Break line of sight first, then hide: wanted levels drain when the law cannot see you, so sprint the route, duck into cover or a quiet road, and let the stars bleed out while you stay boring and stationary.

Keep your partner with you through the whole fade: a partner left behind, switched away from or lost mid-escape risks the together condition, so drive one car, make one plan, and finish it as the duo the trophy describes.

If the escape collapses, laugh and restage it: the setup takes minutes, the police hold no grudges between attempts, and the run where the route finally flows clean is exactly the run the trophy was waiting for.
trophies.tip: Four stars, partner aboard, planned route, hide till clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner, without the wanted level ever fully clearing between them — a chained crime spree with the heat held, not lost. Plan the chain before the first robbery: pick three shops within a short drive of each other, stage a fast car, and move shop to shop while the stars stay lit. The failure mode is dawdling — a wanted level that drains to zero mid-chain breaks the run — so keep momentum, rob briskly, and let the third shop's escape be the one where you finally vanish.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); wanted system: series precedent from GTA V, applied in this guide's method
strategy: Plan the whole chain before robbing anything: choose three shops a short drive apart, learn the route between them, and stage your fastest reliable car — this trophy is won in the planning, not the robbing.
Bring your partner and keep them close: the chain must be robbed together, so both protagonists ride the same car and enter each shop as a pair, never splitting up to save thirty seconds.

Move briskly and keep the stars alive: the chain breaks if your wanted level fully clears between shops, so drive directly, rob efficiently and re-offend promptly — momentum is literally the mechanic being tested.

Rob each shop the same clean way: in, demand, till, out, gone — improvisation inside a shop wastes the seconds the wanted level needs to stay lit, and a fumbled robbery invites a star level you did not plan for.

After the third till, disappear properly: now the escape is the job, so run your best route, break line of sight and hide until the heat dies — the trophy pays when the chain and the escape are both complete.
trophies.tip: Three shops, one unbroken heat — plan the chain first.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover one hundred different vehicles — models, not individual cars, so the hundredth sedan of a type you know adds nothing. The discovery habit is simple: whenever a vehicle you do not recognise crosses your path, get in it or register it, because discovery in this series is counted by variety encountered up close. Wealthy districts, the airport, marinas and industrial yards each stock different slices of the catalogue. The stats screen tracks your discovered count; the last twenty models are always the rare ones, so hunt those by habitat, not by luck.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 100 vehicles); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Chase variety, not volume: the counter reads discovered models, so the tenth example of a car you know is worthless while one odd truck in a yard is gold — train your eye for silhouettes you have not sat in yet.

Get close enough to register each find: discovery means encountering the vehicle properly — in it, or registered through the game's systems — so do not assume a distant sighting counted; check the counter move when it matters.

Hunt by habitat: rich districts stock the exotics, the airport and docks stock the working fleets, industrial yards and the rural interior stock the oddballs — a district tour with discovery in mind fills whole families per trip.

Pair discovery with the Scooter Bros registrations: the ten vehicles that app trophy needs are ten discoveries too, so register first and discover simultaneously, and let the two exploration counters share every mile.

Expect the last twenty to be rare and plan for them: check the stats screen, note which families are missing, and visit the habitats that stock them at the times they spawn — rarity is a schedule, not a mystery.
trophies.tip: A hundred models — hunt variety by habitat, not by luck.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Five enemies down inside one Combat Focus activation — a positioning trophy wearing a shooting trophy's clothes. Find a moment with at least five enemies visible together: a robbery gone loud, a gang operation's courtyard, a mission ambush. Enter focus with a loaded, accurate weapon, pick targets nearest to furthest, and let the slow time do the aiming. If a crowd thins before you are ready, manufacture one — noise draws enemies together. Practise the activation on four-target groups until the rhythm is calm, then take the real attempt.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); combat systems: series precedent from GTA V's special abilities, applied in this guide's method
strategy: Set the stage before touching the ability: you need five or more enemies alive, visible and reasonably grouped when focus starts, so find or manufacture a crowd — a loud robbery or a gang courtyard both provide one.

Enter focus loaded and settled: full magazine, an accurate mid-range weapon in hand, your aim already resting on the first target — the activation window is generous only to hunters who start it prepared.

Work nearest to furthest in one calm sweep: drop the closest threat first and walk your aim outward, letting the slowed time do what it is for, instead of snapping between distant targets and wasting the window.

Practise on smaller groups until the rhythm is boring: four-target activations teach the pacing without the pressure, and the five-target attempt should feel like the practice with one extra guest, not a new sport.

If the window closes at four, reset without frustration: crowds respawn, robberies recur, and the attempt where positioning, weapon and calm finally coincide tends to arrive within a handful of honest tries.
trophies.tip: Five in one focus — positioning first, calm sweep second.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the airport you learned during the VCIA Takedown mission. In plain terms: get airborne from the airport in a way the airport did not schedule, which means reaching a plane, taking off and leaving the field under your own power, most naturally with the law or the airport objecting. Scout the airfield in free roam first, choose your aircraft and your runway line in daylight and calm, and make the departure clean — the trophy wants the departure, not a fireball on the perimeter road.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); airport layout: Rockstar's official Leonida pages and this guide's playthrough notes
strategy: Scout VCIA in free roam before attempting anything: find where aircraft sit, which service roads reach them unobserved and which runway line gives you the longest clean run — the mission taught you this ground, now learn its gaps.

Pick your moment like a professional: daylight, a quiet apron and an aircraft you can actually fly are worth more than bravado — the trophy asks for a departure, and a calm theft beats a spectacular explosion.

Commit once you move: reach the aircraft directly, start it, taxi the shortest honest line to a runway and climb out — hesitation on an airfield is what turns an unscheduled departure into an unscheduled arrest.

Expect attention and ignore it gracefully: if the departure draws a wanted level, keep climbing and leave the airport's sky; the trophy is about the leaving, and the heat can be lost later, somewhere far from VCIA.

If the attempt ends in the fence, walk away and re-scout: airfields are patient places, aircraft respawn, and the second attempt with a better aircraft position chosen is usually the one that leaves Leonida beautifully.
trophies.tip: Scout the airfield, steal calmly, climb out — departure done.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is the instruction: it gets hot in a Rhino, so get into a Rhino tank and make it hot — survive the military attention a stolen tank inevitably attracts. Rhinos live where the military keeps them, so this trophy begins as a theft: reach the vehicle, take it, and then endure the escalating response long enough for the trophy to register the situation. Armour is the whole point of the vehicle, so trust it, keep moving, and do not abandon the tank at the first sign of trouble — heat is the requirement, not the failure.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); vehicle precedent: the Rhino tank across the GTA series, per this guide's method notes
strategy: Start with the theft, planned like any other: Rhinos are kept by people with guns and fences, so scout the approach, pick your entry and exit, and accept that the drive out is the hardest part of the whole trophy.

Once you are in the armour, trust the armour: a Rhino's entire purpose is absorbing the attention it attracts, so keep rolling, keep your line simple and do not abandon the vehicle when the situation first gets loud.

Make it hot, as the description insists: the trophy wants the heat a tank generates — military attention, a serious wanted response — so engage the situation rather than hiding from it in a quiet corner of the map.

Manage the vehicle's health like a resource: avoid the few threats that genuinely hurt armour, use the cannon to keep distance from them, and remember a destroyed Rhino pays nothing but a long walk home.
