When the trophy lands, enjoy the exit strategy of your choice: outrun the heat, hide the tank somewhere absurd, or go down in legend — the award is already banked, and everything after it is pure sandbox joy.
trophies.tip: Steal a Rhino, trust the armour, welcome the heat.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — the robbery circuit's stealth exam. Undetected is the whole trophy: no alarms tripped by sloppiness, no witnesses free to call it in, in and out like weather. Scout your store first in daylight as a customer: entrances, staff positions, the quiet way out. Enter prepared, move deliberately, control the room without noise, take the goods and leave by the route you chose. A detected attempt costs nothing but time — stores reset, so rehearse the route on failures until the silent run feels ordinary.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); stealth method: this guide's robbery-circuit playtesting notes
strategy: Scout the store as a customer first: walk in during the day, note the entrances, the staff, where the goods sit and which exit is quietest — a silent robbery is designed in the scouting, executed in the visit.

Choose your moment and your store deliberately: fewer witnesses and a clean getaway line matter more than the size of the take, because the trophy pays for undetected, not for rich — pick the beatable shop, not the famous one.

Move like weather once inside: deliberate, quiet, no wasted gestures — control the room without noise, keep every witness accounted for, and never let the situation improvise a louder plan than the one you brought.

Take the goods and leave by the chosen route, unhurried: detection usually happens in the exit, when greed or panic makes hunters sprint past the one person they forgot — walk out as calmly as you walked in.

Treat detections as rehearsals, not failures: the store resets, the route knowledge stays, and each loud attempt teaches one more detail — the silent run, when it comes, will feel almost disappointingly easy.
trophies.tip: Scout it as a customer; rob it like weather — silent.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape from each — the robbery circuit's silver. Each vault is a complete job: entry, vault work, a hot exit and a clean disappearance, and an escape only counts when the heat is truly lost. Standardise your method across all five: same preparation ritual, same escape discipline, a planned route away from every bank before you enter it. Banks differ in layout and response, so scout each one, but the ritual should not change — consistency is what turns five heists into a routine instead of five adventures.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 5 vaults); method: this guide's robbery-circuit playtesting notes
strategy: Build one ritual and use it five times: scout the bank, plan the escape route before entering, rob with the same calm sequence, run the route, hide until clear — a repeated ritual turns five heists into one skill.

Plan the escape before the robbery, every time: know your first three turns out of the bank's street, your line-of-sight break and your hiding ground before you ever touch the vault, because escapes improvised under stars fail.

Count only clean finishes: a vault robbed but an escape blown is a rehearsal, not a withdrawal, so if the exit collapses, survive or reload and rerun the whole job properly rather than counting a mess.

Vary the banks, not the method: five different vaults teach you the circuit's range — layouts, response times, neighbourhood geometry — while your unchanging ritual keeps each new job feeling familiar by the door.

Rest between heists like a professional: bank the money, lose the heat fully, repair your life and your car, and only then scout the next vault — the fifth bank falls to patience far more than to daring.
trophies.tip: Five vaults, one ritual — escape planned before entry.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — a classic, as the name says. Armored trucks run routes through Leonida; the job is to stop one, open it, take the money and vanish before the response organises. Choose your ambush ground with the escape already in mind: a place the truck can be stopped, worked on briefly and left from quickly. The truck's armour dictates the method — you need the means to open it, so arrive equipped rather than hopeful. Once the money is yours, the escape is the trophy: lose the heat completely.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's robbery-circuit playtesting notes
strategy: Find a truck and follow it before touching it: armored trucks run learnable routes, and two minutes of patient tailing tells you where it slows, where it turns and where its escort attention is thinnest.

Choose ambush ground that is really escape ground: a stop point with a fast exit, a line-of-sight break within seconds and no crowd — the robbery takes a moment, the escape takes the whole neighbourhood.

Arrive equipped to open armour: the truck will not yield to wishes, so bring whatever the game provides for breaching it, tested beforehand if possible — experimenting with explosives beside the target is a genre of failure.

Work fast and leave faster: the moment the money is in hand, the job changes from robbery to disappearance — run the planned route, break sight, hide, and let the stars drain before you even count the take.

If the first truck gets away or the escape collapses, simply find the next one: trucks are a system, not a unique event, and the hunter who treats attempts as routine will rob one cleanly within the hour.
trophies.tip: Tail it, stop it on escape ground, open it, vanish.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — reveal the whole state, every district, island, swamp road and mountain shoulder. The map fills as you genuinely visit ground, so work it systematically: region by region, coastlines and interiors both, using the exploration phase's other hunts — meditation spots, stunts, discoveries — as the excuse that takes you everywhere anyway. The last unrevealed patches are always the unglamorous ones: a swamp track, an island's far shore, a service road. When the map looks complete but the trophy has not landed, sweep the edges.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's region-by-region exploration sweep
strategy: Work the state region by region with the map open: reveal each district fully — coast, interior, islands and high ground — before moving on, so the exploration phase's single pass leaves no fog pockets behind you.

Let the other hunts carry you: meditation spots, stunt clusters, strand journeys and vehicle habitats already visit most of Leonida, so schedule this trophy as their passenger and only drive dedicated miles for the gaps.

Respect the unglamorous ground: the last unrevealed percent is never a famous beach — it is a swamp track, a mangrove channel, an island's far shore, a service road behind somewhere you have been ten times.

Use every vehicle class the state offers: some Leonida only reveals from the water or the air, so when land routes stop filling the map, take a boat along the coast and a plane over the interior and watch the fog retreat.

When the map looks complete and the trophy disagrees, sweep the edges at low zoom: compare the revealed map against the state's outline district by district, and the missing smudge will show itself to a patient eye.
trophies.tip: Reveal everything — the last fog hides on swamp tracks.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — one per gang, across all of Leonida's factions. The work is intelligence first: learn which operations belong to which gang, because robbing the same gang twice pays once. Each operation is a defended workplace, so scout its approaches, choose your entry, rob it and get clear; the Combat Focus and robbery skills from the rest of the circuit all apply. Keep a written tally by gang name in the tracker — this trophy is lost in bookkeeping more often than in gunfire.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); method: this guide's robbery-circuit playtesting notes
strategy: Do the intelligence work first: learn Leonida's gangs and which illegal operations belong to each, because the trophy counts gangs robbed, not operations — a second robbery of the same colours pays nothing at all.

Keep a tally by gang name in the tracker, updated the day each job lands: this is the one combat trophy that is genuinely lost in bookkeeping, with hunters re-robbing a familiar gang while a stranger gang waits untouched.

Scout each operation like a workplace, because it is one: approaches, guards' rhythm, where the money or product sits, and the way out that does not pass the front door — then rob it on your plan, not its surprises.

Bring the full circuit toolkit: Combat Focus for the crowded moment, a planned escape route for the exit, and the discipline to leave the moment the take is secured rather than looting a defended building for pleasure.

Space the jobs across the combat phase: one gang's operation per session keeps each robbery fresh and well-scouted, and by the last gang your method will be so practised that the hardest part is remembering to tick it off.
trophies.tip: One operation per gang — tally by name, not by count.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, get a cocktail, and enjoy it with the view — the ellipsis in the description is the game savouring the moment, and so should you. This is the list's postcard trophy: find the beachfront spot where a drink can be had, order it, and let the scene play. No timer, no skill, no danger beyond sunburn. Take it early as a breather between heavier hunts, or save it as a ritual — many hunters make it the last bronze before the platinum, a drink at the end of the long road.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); location: Rockstar's official Leonida pages on Vice City and Ocean Beach
strategy: Go to Ocean Beach and find where a cocktail can be had: the beachfront is the game's postcard, and the drinking spot sits in its social heart — walk the strip like a tourist until the prompt presents itself.

Order the drink and actually enjoy the view: the trophy is a moment, not a transaction, so let the scene play out fully rather than skipping ahead — the game built this pause on purpose, inside a list of chaos.
Take it whenever the hunt needs a breath: at ten to twenty minutes with no fail state at all, this bronze is the perfect palate cleanser between a failed heist chain and whatever you attempt next.
Or save it as a ritual, as many hunters do: the final light trophy before the platinum, a cocktail on Ocean Beach with fifty-three trophies banked and the end genuinely in sight across the water.
Tick it off with uncharacteristic sentimentality and move on: not every trophy must be earned at gunpoint, and remembering that is worth exactly one bronze, paid by the state of Leonida itself.
trophies.tip: Ocean Beach, one cocktail, enjoy the view — a postcard.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, in classic style — meaning: take a car from inside the showroom and exit through the glass, not the door. Find a showroom with display cars, choose the one you fancy, get in and drive it out through the window in one committed motion. Classic style is commitment: half-hearted nudges at the glass just embarrass everyone. The trophy pays on the smash itself; whatever wanted level follows is a separate, ordinary problem with ordinary solutions.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); series precedent: showroom escapes are a GTA tradition, per this guide's method notes
strategy: Find a vehicle showroom and walk in like a customer: look at the display cars, note which one faces the glass with a run-up behind it, and pick your exit line before you pick your car.

Choose the car you actually want to keep: you are about to own it in the most literal way, so let taste decide — classic style begins with stealing the vehicle you would have bought in a kinder world.

Commit to the glass completely: build what speed the floor allows, aim for the centre of the largest pane and drive through without lifting off — hesitation at the window is the only way this trophy goes wrong.
Land the exit cleanly and keep driving: the smash is the trophy, the aftermath is just a wanted level, so treat the first thirty seconds outside as an ordinary escape and lose the heat ordinarily.

If the first showroom's geometry defeats you, find another: Leonida sells cars in more than one glass box, and the showroom whose floor plan suits a run-up will make the whole thing feel like a film scene.
trophies.tip: In like a customer, out through the glass — commit fully.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl — the follow-through is the game's wink at the series' oldest social ritual. Find the alley, play a game properly: shoes, lane, full frames, honest follow-through on every throw. The trophy asks for the activity completed, not a score, so a gutter-heavy game bowled in good faith counts exactly as much as a perfect one. Take it during the activity lap and enjoy the fact that the most feared phone call in GTA history is now a trophy with your name invited.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); location naming: as published in the official list
strategy: Find the Kolt & Associates alley and take a lane: this is an activity trophy, earned by bowling at the named place, so the journey is the address — everything after arrival is just a pleasant game.

Play the game properly and completely: full frames, honest throws, a real follow-through on each delivery as the description requests — a half-abandoned game helps nobody, and the trophy respects completion.

Do not chase a score that nobody asked for: the award ignores your total entirely, so a cheerful game full of gutter balls, bowled in good faith to the final frame, pays the identical bronze to a strike-fest.

Fold it into the activity lap: the alley visit belongs naturally beside the arcade completion and the first range attempts, and banking three light activities in one outing is Phase 3 at its most efficient.
Tick it, and spare a thought for the series' history: bowling invitations were once the most dreaded sound in Liberty City — here, for once, you get to be the one who insists on going.
trophies.tip: Find the alley, bowl a full game, follow through.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — the vaguest description on the list, and deliberately so: this is the duo's crowd-pleasing moment, earned by performing together where Leonida can see it. Play it as the partner phase teaches: with Lucia and Jason together, take the partnership into the public, performative corners of the game — the shared activities and spectacles the two protagonists can do as a pair — and the moment the game recognises as the partnership's crowd-pleaser will land it. If an attempt does not register, vary the stage, not the partnership.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); interpretation: this guide's partner-phase method notes
strategy: Read the description as a stage direction: a partnership with mass appeal is the duo performing together in public, so bring both protagonists and look for the game's shared, performative moments rather than private ones.

Work through the pair's joint repertoire systematically: the activities and spectacles Lucia and Jason can do together are a finite list, and the crowd-pleaser the trophy wants lives somewhere inside it — try them as a pair, in public, one by one.

Keep the duo together for the whole attempt: like the other partner trophies, the together condition is the soul of the thing, so no splitting up, no solo shortcuts, no leaving one protagonist parked across town.

Vary the stage when an attempt does not register, not the partnership: a different venue, a different shared activity, a bigger crowd — the trophy is a recognition moment, and recognition depends on where the performance happens.

When it lands, note exactly where and how in the tracker: the vaguest trophy on the list is the one future-you will least remember solving, and a two-line note turns tonight's discovery into permanent knowledge.
trophies.tip: The duo, together, in public — vary the stage till it lands.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. This trophy turns on a single story choice — choices made, for better or worse — and a playthrough that passes the moment the wrong way cannot earn it without returning. The protection is the roadmap's oldest rule: keep a manual save from just before the choice, in its own slot, and the miss costs a reload instead of a second playthrough. When the story offers you a decision that feels weighted, save first and choose second; if the trophy does not follow the choice you made, reload and choose the other way.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); protection method: this guide's chapter-break save rule
strategy: Know before you arrive that this one can be missed: it turns on a single story choice, and a playthrough that sails past the moment wrongly has no way back except a save — so the whole strategy is the save, made early.

Bank a manual save in its own slot whenever the story starts to feel weighted: decisions that matter announce themselves by tone long before they announce themselves by consequence, and a save costs thirty seconds.

At the choice itself, save once more if the game allows, then choose with your whole chest: the description's shrug — for better or worse — hints the trophy respects commitment to a decision, whichever one you make.

If the trophy does not follow your choice, do not panic and do not start a new game: reload the save you banked, take the moment the other way, and watch whether the bronze prefers the road not taken.

Once it lands, protect the save until the platinum is done: this trophy is the list's standing lesson in why the chapter-break scheme exists, and the hunters who sneer at save discipline are the ones replaying campaigns.
trophies.tip: MISSABLE — save before the big choice; reload beats replay.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. Second time's the charm: this trophy needs a specific moment to go wrong first and right second — fail once, then succeed at the same thing. The missable trap is succeeding too well: a hunter who nails the moment first try has nothing to retry. The protection is a save banked before the moment, so the sequence can be arranged deliberately: attempt, fail honestly, succeed on the return. If you are not sure which moment it is, save before anything that smells like a one-shot test, and arrange the fail-then-succeed order on purpose.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); protection method: this guide's chapter-break save rule
strategy: Understand the shape before the moment arrives: this trophy wants a failure followed by a success at the same test — second time's the charm — so a flawless first attempt is, uniquely, the way to miss it.

Bank a save before anything that smells like a one-shot test: a trial, an audition, a single staged attempt the story frames as mattering — thirty seconds of saving buys you control over the order of events.

Fail the first attempt honestly when the moment comes: no trophy in history has asked less of you, so resist every instinct, let the attempt go wrong in the ordinary way, and make sure the game registers the failure.

Then succeed on the immediate return: same test, second try, charm working — the pairing of a registered failure and a following success is the whole recipe, and it must be the same moment, not two unrelated ones.

If you accidentally succeeded first try somewhere suspicious, reload the banked save and do it in the right order: this is exactly the accident the save scheme exists for, and it costs minutes instead of a campaign.
trophies.tip: MISSABLE — fail it once on purpose, then succeed. Save first.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Something strange is in Leonida's skies and swamps, and this trophy is for witnessing it: what the hell just happened is the correct response to the game's weirdest encounter. Hunt it like every series mystery before it — follow the odd reports the world drops, visit the remote places at the hours when nothing sensible happens, and be somewhere lonely when the strangeness arrives. There is no marker and no schedule you can brute-force; the encounter rewards the explorer who wanders the wild interior after dark with their eyes genuinely open.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); mystery tradition: the GTA series' long-running strange-encounter easter eggs, per this guide's method notes
strategy: Accept the genre: this is the list's mystery trophy, an encounter the game hides in its strangest corners, and it will not be found by following markers — it is found by wandering with intent.

Listen to the world's odd reports as you travel: strangers, radio chatter and local colour in this series have always pointed, however obliquely, at where the weirdness lives — treat throwaway lines as field intelligence.

Work the lonely places at lonely hours: the remote interior, the deep swamp, the empty Keys at night — strangeness in Leonida keeps the same hours and postcodes it always has, far from the neon and the crowds.

When something impossible happens, stay and witness it fully: the trophy wants the encounter experienced, not glimpsed, so do not drive away from the strangest moment of your entire hunt — stand in it until it concludes.

If the skies stay silent, change one variable at a time — place, hour, weather of the world — and keep a note of where you have waited: even a mystery yields to a methodical hunter eventually, and your notes are the method.
trophies.tip: The weird encounter — lonely places, late hours, eyes open.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, strike pedestrians or targets with a melee weapon out the window and drop them like pins — a group flattened in one pass is the image the name is painting. Set it up where people gather in a line or a cluster the car can pass closely: a queue, a boardwalk crowd, a sidewalk stream. Arm the melee weapon before the pass, drive the line at the right speed — fast enough to be a drive-by, slow enough to connect — and let the physics do the bowling.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); series precedent: melee drive-by mechanics from GTA V, per this guide's method notes
strategy: Find your pins first: a line or cluster of people the car can pass at arm's length — a queue, a crowded boardwalk, a busy sidewalk — because a melee drive-by needs targets arranged the way the trophy's name arranges them.
Arm the melee weapon before the pass begins: the strike must come from the moving vehicle, so set your weapon, pick your line and commit — fumbling with equipment mid-pass is how pins survive.

Drive the line at connecting speed: too fast and the swing whistles past, too slow and it is no longer a drive-by — the right pace feels like a parade float with intent, close enough for every pin to be reachable.

Take the whole cluster in one pass if the ground allows: the trophy's heart is the strike — several down in a single sweep — so a pass that clips one person at a time is practice, not the attempt itself.

Expect the wanted level and plan the shrug: bowling with a car attracts attention, so know your exit before the pass, and once the trophy lands, lose the heat the ordinary way and go tick a very silly bronze.
trophies.tip: Line up the pins, melee armed, one sweeping drive-by.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn a quarter of a million dollars laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. This is a pipeline trophy: marked bills come from the criminal economy — robberies, operations, the grey work of the combat phase — and leave as clean money through your contacts, at the dime-on-the-dollar rate the name quotes. Build the pipeline early, feed it from every heist and operation the hunt already runs, and never let marked bills sit unlaundered in a drawer. The stats screen counts laundered earnings exactly; reconcile weekly and the quarter million arrives on schedule.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — $250,000 laundered); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Build the pipeline in the combat phase, not after it: marked bills flow from robberies and illegal operations, and your contacts turn them clean — a pipeline built early launders the whole hunt's takings, not a desperate endgame pile.
Feed it from work you already do: every vault, truck and gang operation in Phase 5 generates the raw material, so route the proceeds through your contacts as a ritual, the same day they are earned.

Never let marked bills sit idle: unlaundered money in a drawer is progress frozen at zero, so make laundering part of the post-heist routine — escape, hide, launder, save — until the sequence runs itself.

Reconcile against the stats screen weekly: the counter is exact and the target is large, and a hunter watching the number climb past fifty, a hundred, two hundred thousand never faces the shock of a stalled pipeline at the end.

If the count lags late, run the pipeline deliberately: a few sessions of operation robberies aimed purely at marked bills, laundered immediately, will close a five-figure gap faster than any single score in the game.
trophies.tip: Build the laundry pipeline early; launder after every job.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a hundred thousand dollars across all shops — the friendliest grind on the list, because the hunt makes you rich and Leonida makes spending easy. The discipline is simply not to hoard: buy the vehicles, clothes, weapons, armour and services the hunt actually wants, when it wants them, and the counter fills as a by-product of playing well-equipped. Across all shops is the only nuance — spread the spending around the state's tills rather than emptying one store. The stats screen counts it; check before any endgame splurge so the splurge is aimed.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — $100,000 spent); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Simply refuse to hoard: the hunt makes you wealthy, and this trophy asks you to live like it — buy the cars, clothes, weapons, armour and tune-ups the hunt genuinely wants, at the moment it wants them.
Spread the spending across all shops, as the description specifies: Leonida's tills are many, so shop around the state rather than emptying one store — variety is both the rule and the pleasure here.

Let big purchases do the heavy lifting honestly: garages, serious vehicles and full loadouts move the counter in thousands at a time, and they are purchases the roadmap recommends anyway for the endgame's comfort.

Check the counter before any planned splurge: the stats screen tells you exactly how far from a hundred thousand you stand, so a late-game buying session can be aimed to finish the trophy rather than overshooting blindly.

When it lands, notice what it taught you: a platinum hunter who equips properly all game is faster, safer and richer than a miser on a pile of unspent cash — this bronze is the list's reward for playing generously.
trophies.tip: Spend as you hunt, across all shops — do not hoard.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase every garage property in Leonida. This is a money-and-map trophy: garages sit across the state, each with its price, and owning them all takes the wealth the combat and grind phases generate. Buy them as the money allows rather than saving for a single spree — each garage is also a working asset, storage and a safe point in its district, so early purchases pay rent in convenience. Keep a district-by-district list of what you own; the last unpurchased garage is always the one in the district you visit least.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade); progress: the in-game stats and property records
strategy: List them all before buying any: garages are scattered across the state's districts at different prices, so make the full list first — an unlisted garage cannot be bought, and the last one is always in your least-visited district.

Buy as the money allows instead of saving for one spree: each garage works for its living immediately — storage, a safe point, a district foothold — so early purchases pay rent in convenience all hunt long.

Fund them from the honest economy: heist proceeds, laundered money and activity winnings are the income the roadmap builds, and a garage bought with the hunt's own earnings is the money trophies working exactly as designed.

Keep the owned list current in the tracker, district by district: property bookkeeping fails quietly, and the hunter who ticks purchases the day they happen never faces the endgame tour of every for-sale sign in Leonida.

When one garage remains, treat its purchase as a small ceremony: it completes the property set, usually completes a healthy slice of the spending counter too, and marks the moment the hunt's economy is fully built.
trophies.tip: Every garage, bought as money allows — list them first.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — ten different vehicles, registered through the app as you encounter them. Make it a reflex from the first hour: any vehicle you climb into that the app has not seen gets registered on the spot, which is precisely what the trophy's name is telling you to do. Ten is a small number spread across a hundred hours of driving, so the only way to make this trophy hard is to ignore the app until the end and then hunt ten vehicles in a car park. Register early, register everything, finish incidentally.
trophies.source: Official PS5 trophy list (name, description, grade — count 10 vehicles); progress: the in-game stats screen
strategy: Register on the spot, as the name commands: from the first hour, any vehicle you climb into that the app has not seen gets registered immediately, before the drive, while the novelty is still in your hands.

Chase ten different vehicles, not ten registrations of a favourite: the counter wants variety on the app's books, so let taxis, trucks, boats-adjacent oddballs and one memorable supercar all take their turn.

Pair it with the hundred-vehicle discovery hunt: every registration is also a discovery, so the two exploration counters share the same encounters and the same miles — work them together or pay for the travel twice.
Use mission and strand vehicles too: borrowed cars count their moment just as owned ones do, so register the interesting metal the story hands you before returning it to the plot.

Check the count whenever you open the app: ten is small enough to finish almost by accident, and the hunter who glances at the number in week one is never the hunter hunting a tenth vehicle in the finale week.
trophies.tip: Register each new vehicle on the spot — ten, done early.
